upsertPapers.title: Optimal Clustering with Noisy Queries via Multi-Armed Bandit

upsertSlices.label: Clustering from noisy labels: recovery and query cost
upsertSlices.task: Persistent noise, a tight fixed-noise reference, and the full accuracy dependence.
assumptions: This is planted-partition recovery, distinct from minimizing disagreements. The fixed reference matches output promises; the tradeoff panel labels large-cluster and exact-recovery results separately. Symbolic columns are not a numerical frontier.

axis.label: See scoped figure panels; incompatible objectives have separate axes

categories.label: Persistent noisy pair queries · balanced two clusters

results.guarantee: Recover both hidden clusters with probability 1−o(1)
results.notes: For fixed k=2 and δ=1/16, linear-size clusters exceed the required Ω(k⁴log n/δ²) threshold; the additive log³n term is asymptotically dominated.

results.guarantee: Exact recovery with success at least 15/16 on balanced inputs
results.notes: §5 hard distribution assigns independent fair cluster labels. Balance fails with probability≤2exp(−n/18). Conditioning with success slack preserves the 7/8 distributional lower bound; cached distinct queries bound off-promise work by n². This balanced-promise statement is an explicit elementary corollary, not a literal theorem quotation. A hypothetical o(n log n)-query algorithm is truncated after n² queries, with o(1) extra failure by Markov; off-promise work is then bounded.

results.guarantee: Recover every cluster of size≥Ω(k⁴log n/δ²)
results.notes: The two terms retain full δ dependence. This is not unconditional exact recovery of all cluster sizes.

results.bound: Ω(n log n / δ²) expected queries
results.notes: Displayed δ range follows the proof. Do not extrapolate this noisy-query lower bound to δ=1 or compare its exact-recovery contract indiscriminately with large-cluster-only recovery.
